summary: cutsq_custom is declared as int instead of double, so the trim cutoff squared is truncated to an integer and neighbors are dropped (or all of them dropped when the cutoff is below 1.0).
evidence: src/KOKKOS/npair_skip_kokkos.h:283 'int nlocal,num_skip,cutsq_custom;'.  It is filled with a floating point value in src/KOKKOS/npair_skip_kokkos.cpp:50 'cutsq_custom = cutoff_custom*cutoff_custom;' and compared against a double in :144 'if (rsq > cutsq_custom) continue;'.  Every other npair trim class stores it as double: src/KOKKOS/npair_trim_kokkos.h:248 'double cutsq_custom;', src/KOKKOS/npair_halffull_kokkos.h:366 'double cutsq_custom,delta;', src/npair_skip.cpp:68 'double cutsq_custom = cutoff_custom * cutoff_custom;'.
failure_scenario: skip/trim/kk/* list with cutoff_custom = 3.5 -> cutsq_custom = int(12.25) = 12, so neighbor pairs at 3.465 < r <= 3.5 A are silently dropped from the list; with cutoff_custom < 1.0 (e.g. a short-range fix list) cutsq_custom becomes 0 and the list is emptied entirely, zeroing all forces from that sub-style.
suggested_fix: Change the declaration to 'int nlocal,num_skip; double cutsq_custom;'.

summary: build() writes d_ilist on the device but never calls k_list->k_ilist.modify<DeviceType>(), so a later k_ilist.sync_host() is a no-op and consumers read stale host ilist data.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/npair_skip_kokkos.cpp:151 'd_ilist(inum) = i;' (device kernel) and the end of build() at :97-105 has no modify call.  Every other KOKKOS npair build does it: src/KOKKOS/npair_kokkos.cpp:360 'list->k_ilist.template modify<DeviceType>();', src/KOKKOS/npair_halffull_kokkos.cpp:82, src/KOKKOS/npair_ssa_kokkos.cpp:520, src/KOKKOS/npair_trim_kokkos.cpp:84.  Consumers rely on the flag: src/KOKKOS/npair_copy_kokkos.cpp:77 and src/KOKKOS/npair_trim_kokkos.cpp:130 call 'listcopy_kk->k_ilist.sync_host()' before reading view_host(), as does src/KOKKOS/fix_reaxff_species_kokkos.cpp:80.
failure_scenario: A CPU-side list copied or trimmed from a skip/kk/device list (kk2cpu path in NPairCopyKokkos::copy_to_cpu / NPairTrimKokkos::trim_to_cpu), or fix reaxff/species, reads the host mirror of k_ilist, which still contains whatever the last host-side write left (all zeros on the first build) -> wrong atom indices, wrong neighbor lists, likely out-of-bounds firstneigh entries.
suggested_fix: Add 'k_list->k_ilist.template modify<DeviceType>();' at the end of NPairSkipKokkos::build(), as the sibling npair styles do.

summary: NPairTrimKokkos's constructor never sets execution_space, so it keeps the NPair default of Host and the device build syncs x to the host instead of the device.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/npair_trim_kokkos.cpp:27 'NPairTrimKokkos<DeviceType>::NPairTrimKokkos(LAMMPS *lmp) : NPair(lmp) {}' - no 'execution_space = ExecutionSpaceFromDevice<DeviceType>::space;'.  The base sets 'execution_space = Host;' in src/npair.cpp:44.  The sibling styles do set it: src/KOKKOS/npair_halffull_kokkos.cpp:33 and src/KOKKOS/npair_skip_kokkos.cpp:28.  It is then used in src/KOKKOS/npair_trim_kokkos.cpp:57 'atomKK->sync(execution_space,X_MASK);' immediately before the device kernel that reads 'x = atomKK->k_x.view<DeviceType>()' (:56, kernel at :94-111).
failure_scenario: With trim/kk/device, whenever x was last modified on the host (host-side comm/exchange/borders, a non-Kokkos fix touching x, read_restart) the device copy of x is never refreshed; the trim kernel computes rsq from stale coordinates and keeps/drops the wrong neighbors, giving wrong forces without any error.  It also forces a pointless device->host copy of x on every build.
suggested_fix: Set 'execution_space = ExecutionSpaceFromDevice<DeviceType>::space;' in the NPairTrimKokkos constructor.

summary: xprd_half/yprd_half/zprd_half are stored as int in NeighborKokkosExecute, truncating the half box lengths and corrupting minimum_image_check(), which decides whether special-bond scaling is applied to a pair.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/npair_kokkos.h:261 'const int xprd_half, yprd_half, zprd_half;' with the matching constructor parameters at :303 'const int & _xprd_half, const int & _yprd_half, const int & _zprd_half'.  They are initialized in src/KOKKOS/npair_kokkos.cpp:206 from 'domain->xprd_half,domain->yprd_half,domain->zprd_half', which are declared 'double xprd_half, yprd_half, zprd_half;' in src/domain.h:50.  They are then used in floating point comparisons: src/KOKKOS/npair_kokkos.h:420-425 'if (xperiodic && fabs(dx) > xprd_half) return 1;', which must match src/domain.h:198-204 exactly.
failure_scenario: Box with xprd = 9.0 -> domain->xprd_half = 4.5 but the functor stores 4.  A 1-4 special-bond partner whose |dx| is 4.2 makes minimum_image_check() return 1 on the KOKKOS path and 0 on the CPU path, so the pair is stored without the special-bond code and the special_lj/special_coul factor is never applied -> wrong energies/forces for molecular systems in small periodic boxes (and every pair in a box shorter than 2 length units, where xprd_half truncates to 0 or 1).
suggested_fix: Change the three members and the three constructor parameters to double.

summary: xprd_half/yprd_half/zprd_half are declared int in NPairSSAKokkosExecute, truncating the half box lengths used by minimum_image_check().
evidence: src/KOKKOS/npair_ssa_kokkos.h:175 'const int xprd_half, yprd_half, zprd_half;' and constructor parameters :237 'const int & _xprd_half, const int & _yprd_half, const int & _zprd_half'; initialized from the doubles 'domain->xprd_half,domain->yprd_half,domain->zprd_half' at src/KOKKOS/npair_ssa_kokkos.cpp:428 (src/domain.h:50 declares them double).  Used in a floating point test at src/KOKKOS/npair_ssa_kokkos.h:342-347, which must match src/domain.h:198-204 as used by the CPU build at src/DPD-REACT/npair_half_bin_newton_ssa.cpp:211 and :296.
failure_scenario: Same as the npair_kokkos.h case: in a box whose half-length is not an integer, special-bond pairs whose |dx| falls between trunc(xprd_half) and xprd_half are stored without the special-bond code and lose their special_lj/special_coul scaling, so SSA/DPD runs disagree with the CPU build.
suggested_fix: Change the three members and the matching constructor parameters to double.

summary: PPPMKokkos does not override reset_grid(), so fix balance drives the inherited PPPM::reset_grid(), which dereferences the base-class gc (always nullptr for the KOKKOS style) and calls the non-virtual PPPM::compute_rho_coeff() on the never-allocated rho_coeff/drho_coeff pointers.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pppm_kokkos.h declares its own shadowing members 'Grid3dKokkos<DeviceType> *gc;' (:449) and a non-virtual 'void compute_rho_coeff();' (:486), while the base declares 'class Grid3d *gc;' (src/KSPACE/pppm.h:84) and the NON-virtual 'void compute_rho_coeff();' (src/KSPACE/pppm.h:142).  PPPMKokkos overrides neither reset_grid() nor allocates the base members, and src/KSPACE/pppm.cpp:637-668 'void PPPM::reset_grid() { deallocate(); ... allocate(); if (!overlap_allowed && !gc->ghost_adjacent()) ...; compute_gf_denom(); ... compute_rho_coeff(); setup(); }'.  The PPPM constructor leaves both at null ('fft1(nullptr), fft2(nullptr), remap(nullptr), gc(nullptr)' and 'rho1d = rho_coeff = drho1d = drho_coeff = nullptr;'), and PPPMKokkos::allocate() (src/KOKKOS/pppm_kokkos.cpp:791-892) only fills the KOKKOS members.  reset_grid() is invoked unconditionally by src/fix_balance.cpp:341 'if (force->kspace) force->kspace->reset_grid();'.
failure_scenario: 'kspace_style pppm/kk' together with 'fix balance ... ' (or any other caller of KSpace::reset_grid): on the first rebalance PPPM::reset_grid() evaluates gc->ghost_adjacent() on a null Grid3d* and then writes rho_coeff[l][m] through a null FFT_SCALAR** -> segmentation fault.
suggested_fix: Add a 'void reset_grid() override;' to PPPMKokkos that repeats the sequence using the KOKKOS members (and make PPPM::compute_rho_coeff() virtual so the KOKKOS version is picked up).

summary: unpack_forward_grid_kokkos's per-atom branch reads the u_brick (per-atom energy) value from d_buf[7*i] without adding unpack_offset, unlike the six virial reads right below it, so the tiled grid comm unpacks the wrong buffer stretch.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pppm_kokkos.cpp:2418 'if (eflag_atom) d_u_brick(iz,iy,ix) = d_buf[7*i];' versus :2420-2425 'd_v0_brick(iz,iy,ix) = d_buf[7*i+1 + unpack_offset]; ... d_v5_brick(iz,iy,ix) = d_buf[7*i+6 + unpack_offset];' and the sibling kernel :2404-2406 'd_vdx_brick(iz,iy,ix) = d_buf[3*i   + unpack_offset];'.  unpack_offset is set from the caller at :2379 and the tiled path passes a non-zero value: src/KOKKOS/grid3d_kokkos.cpp:771-773 'offset = nper * recv[m].offset; kspaceKKBase->unpack_forward_grid_kokkos(which,k_buf2,offset,recv[m].nunpack,k_recv_unpacklist,m);'.  The CPU base advances one running index for every field (src/KSPACE/pppm.cpp, PPPM::unpack_forward_grid, FORWARD_IK_PERATOM branch: 'if (eflag_atom) esrc[list[i]] = buf[n++];').
failure_scenario: comm_style tiled (Comm::LAYOUT_TILED) with 'kspace_style pppm/kk' and any per-atom energy request (compute pe/atom, dump custom c_pe), on a run with more than one received message: every receive after the first fills its ghost u_brick cells from the beginning of the shared receive buffer instead of its own stretch -> wrong per-atom Coulomb energies (and reads past the end of the buffer for the last receive is avoided only by luck).
suggested_fix: Change the line to 'if (eflag_atom) d_u_brick(iz,iy,ix) = d_buf[7*i + unpack_offset];'.

summary: TRIM branch uses cutsq_custom unconditionally and drops the CPU fallback to cutneighsq[itype][jtype], so a trim list whose own request has no custom cutoff (cutoff_custom==0) trims away every neighbor.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/npair_halffull_kokkos.cpp:55 'cutsq_custom = cutoff_custom*cutoff_custom;' and :138/:150 'if (rsq > cutsq_custom) continue;'.  The CPU base src/npair_halffull.cpp:127-128 and :140-141 instead do 'double cutsq_trim = (cutsq_custom > 0.0) ? cutsq_custom : cutneighsq[itype][jtype]; if (rsq > cutsq_trim) continue;'.  The same fallback exists in src/npair_trim.cpp:89 and src/npair_skip.cpp:108.  cutoff_custom is only nonzero when the request set NeighRequest::cut (src/npair.cpp:96), yet Neighbor::morph_halffull()/morph_copy_trim() set trim=1 purely from 'icut != jcut' (src/neighbor.cpp:1495-1501, 1576-1584) where a request without ->cut gets icut = cutneighmax; a parent list requested with a cutoff LARGER than cutneighmax therefore produces a trimmed child whose own cutoff_custom is 0.
failure_scenario: A fix/compute requests a neighbor list with a cutoff larger than the pair-style cutoff+skin (e.g. fix nonaffine/displacement style requests), so the default-cutoff pair list becomes a halffull/trim child of it with cutoff_custom==0.  On CPU it is trimmed back to cutneighsq[itype][jtype]; with KOKKOS cutsq_custom==0 makes 'rsq > 0.0' true for every pair, so every half list is emptied and all pair forces/energies silently become zero.
suggested_fix: Mirror the CPU logic: pass the per-type cutneighsq (as a device dual view) into the functor and use 'const double cutsq_trim = (cutsq_custom > 0.0) ? cutsq_custom : d_cutneighsq(itype,jtype);' , or at minimum error out at build time when TRIM is set and cutoff_custom == 0.

summary: The trim test uses cutsq_custom unconditionally, dropping the CPU fallback to cutneighsq[itype][jtype] when the trimmed list's own request carries no custom cutoff.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/npair_trim_kokkos.cpp:113 'if (rsq > cutsq_custom) continue;' and :179 (CPU path) with cutsq_custom = cutoff_custom*cutoff_custom (:38,:59).  The base src/npair_trim.cpp:89-90 does 'double cutsq_trim = (cutsq_custom > 0.0) ? cutsq_custom : cutneighsq[itype][jtype]; if (rsq > cutsq_trim) continue;'.  cutoff_custom is 0 unless the request set NeighRequest::cut (src/npair.cpp:96), while Neighbor::morph_copy_trim() sets trim=1 from 'icut != jcut' alone (src/neighbor.cpp:1576-1584), where a request without ->cut uses icut = cutneighmax.
failure_scenario: A list with the default cutoff that gets trimmed from a longer-cutoff parent list (parent requested a cutoff larger than cutneighmax) has cutoff_custom == 0, so cutsq_custom == 0 and 'rsq > 0.0' rejects every neighbor -> empty neighbor lists and zero forces, silently.
suggested_fix: Mirror the CPU fallback by passing the per-type cutneighsq into the functor as a device view and using it when cutsq_custom == 0, or refuse to build with an explicit error when TRIM and cutoff_custom == 0.

summary: The TRIM branch drops the CPU fallback to cutneighsq[itype][jtype] when the skip list's own request has no custom cutoff.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/npair_skip_kokkos.cpp:50 'cutsq_custom = cutoff_custom*cutoff_custom;' and :144 'if (rsq > cutsq_custom) continue;' vs src/npair_skip.cpp:108-109 'double cutsq_trim = (cutsq_custom > 0.0) ? cutsq_custom : cutneighsq[itype][jtype]; if (rsq > cutsq_trim) continue;'.  Note src/neighbor.cpp:1244-1252 clears ->cut for skip requests ('skip lists inherit the cutoff of the parent they skip from'), so cutoff_custom is 0 for exactly the skip lists this class builds.
failure_scenario: A skip/trim/kk/* list whose request had its ->cut flag cleared by morph_unique() has cutoff_custom == 0, so every neighbor fails 'rsq > 0.0' and the sub-style's neighbor list is empty; the CPU build of the same input trims to the per-type neighbor cutoffs instead.
suggested_fix: Use the same '(cutsq_custom > 0.0) ? cutsq_custom : cutneighsq[itype][jtype]' rule, with cutneighsq mirrored into a device view.

summary: PPPMKokkos::init() never implements the 'kspace_modify slab auto' iteration, so slab_volfactor stays at its 1.0 initial value and the EW3DC slab correction is applied to a box with no inserted vacuum.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pppm_kokkos.cpp:221-252 runs only the plain 'while (order >= minorder)' loop with no reference to slab_auto, while the CPU base wraps it in the auto-volfactor loop: src/KSPACE/pppm.cpp:295-298 'const bool slab_auto_enabled = (slabflag == 1 && slab_auto); if (slab_auto_enabled) slab_volfactor = auto_slab_volfactor(accuracy, two_charge_force, g_ewald, xprd, yprd, zprd, error);' and :354-360 which re-derives it after adjust_gewald() until converged.  'kspace_modify slab auto' is accepted for any pppmflag style and sets 'slabflag = 1; slab_auto = 1; slab_volfactor = 1.0;' (src/kspace.cpp:527-530); nothing in PPPMKokkos rejects it.
failure_scenario: 'kspace_style pppm/kk' plus 'kspace_modify slab auto': slab_volfactor remains 1.0, so zprd_slab == zprd, Grid3d::set_zfactor(1.0) inserts no vacuum, and slabcorr() adds the EW3DC dipole correction for a slab geometry that was never extended -> silently wrong energies and z forces (the identical CPU input picks a volfactor of typically 3).
suggested_fix: Either port the slab_auto convergence loop from PPPM::init() into PPPMKokkos::init(), or explicitly error out in PPPMKokkos::init() when (slabflag == 1 && slab_auto).

summary: deallocate() nulls fft1 twice and never nulls fft2, leaving fft2 a dangling pointer after the FFT3dKokkos object is deleted.
failure_scenario: Any path that calls deallocate() twice without an intervening allocate() double-frees fft2: e.g. PPPMKokkos::init() calls deallocate() at :212 and error->all()s at :254/:256 before reaching allocate() at :272, after which the destructor (:127) calls deallocate() again -> delete of an already freed FFT3dKokkos.
suggested_fix: Replace the second 'fft1 = nullptr;' with 'fft2 = nullptr;'.

summary: The device find_M kernel drops the CPU check that the two atoms found at tag+1 and tag+2 actually have the TIP4P hydrogen type, so a mis-ordered molecule silently produces a wrong M site instead of an error.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pppm_tip4p_kokkos.cpp:113-122 'int iH1 = AtomKokkos::map_kokkos<DeviceType>(d_tag(i)+1,map_style,k_map_array,k_map_hash); int iH2 = ...(d_tag(i)+2,...); if (iH1 < 0 || iH2 < 0) { k_tip4p_flag...() = 1; ... return; } iH1 = closest_image(i,iH1); iH2 = closest_image(i,iH2);' - only the -1 case is caught.  The CPU base checks both conditions: src/KSPACE/pppm_tip4p.cpp, PPPMTIP4P::find_M(): 'if (iH1 == -1 || iH2 == -1) error->one(FLERR,"TIP4P hydrogen is missing"); if (atom->type[iH1] != typeH || atom->type[iH2] != typeH) error->one(FLERR,"TIP4P hydrogen has incorrect atom type");'.  The same check is present in every other TIP4P implementation (pair_lj_cut_tip4p_long.cpp, pppm_tip4p.cpp).
failure_scenario: A data file whose water molecules are not stored as consecutive O,H,H IDs (e.g. O,H,O,H,... or an ID gap after the O) makes tag+1/tag+2 resolve to non-hydrogen atoms: 'kspace_style pppm/tip4p' aborts with 'TIP4P hydrogen has incorrect atom type', while 'pppm/tip4p/kk' places the M site relative to those unrelated atoms and returns silently wrong long-range energies and forces.
suggested_fix: Add 'if (d_type(iH1) != typeH_kk || d_type(iH2) != typeH_kk) { k_tip4p_flag...() = 2; ... return; }' after the map lookups and report the corresponding error on the host, mirroring the base class.

summary: trim_to_cpu reads atom->x (the host mirror) without syncing X_MASK to the host, so coordinates can be stale when the parent Kokkos list was built on the device.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/npair_trim_kokkos.cpp:130-132 'listcopy_kk->k_ilist.sync_host(); double** x = atom->x;' - k_ilist is synced but nothing calls atomKK->sync(Host,X_MASK), while the distances at :174-177 are computed from that host x.  Compare trim_to_kokkos at :56-57 which does sync x (albeit to the wrong space, see the execution_space finding).
failure_scenario: A non-Kokkos style requesting a trimmed copy of a device-built Kokkos list (kk2cpu + trim) gets its neighbor pairs filtered with host coordinates from the previous device->host sync, so pairs are wrongly kept or dropped after any device-side integration step.
suggested_fix: Call 'atomKK->sync(Host,X_MASK);' at the top of NPairTrimKokkos::trim_to_cpu() before taking atom->x.

summary: For triclinic boxes compute() converts x to lamda coordinates through DomainKokkos, which always runs on the device and marks X_MASK modified on Device, so the pppm/kk/host instantiation keeps reading the un-converted host coordinates.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pppm_kokkos.cpp:590 'x = atomKK->k_x.view<DeviceType>();' and :620 'domain->x2lamda(atomKK->nlocal);' with no atomKK->sync afterwards.  DomainKokkos::x2lamda(int n) (src/KOKKOS/domain_kokkos.cpp:672-685) does 'atomKK->sync(Device,X_MASK); x = atomKK->k_x.view_device(); ... Kokkos::parallel_for(Kokkos::RangePolicy<LMPDeviceType, TagDomain_x2lamda>(0,n),*this); ... atomKK->modified(Device,X_MASK);' - always LMPDeviceType.  src/KOKKOS/pppm_kokkos.h:18 registers 'KSpaceStyle(pppm/kk/host,PPPMKokkos<LMPHostType>);', whose kernels then read the host mirror.
failure_scenario: GPU build, triclinic box, 'kspace_style pppm/kk/host': particle_map()/make_rho()/fieldforce_ik() index the grid with Cartesian coordinates while boxlo has been set to domain->boxlo_lamda (:616-618), so every atom maps to a nonsense grid point -> 'Out of range atoms - cannot compute PPPM' or badly wrong long-range forces.
suggested_fix: Call 'atomKK->sync(execution_space,X_MASK);' after domain->x2lamda() (and again after domain->lamda2x()), or refuse triclinic for the host instantiation.

summary: For NEWTON builds the ghost atoms of the parent full list are looped over and list->gnum is set from the parent, whereas the CPU base restricts both to the newtoff case.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/npair_halffull_kokkos.cpp:61-62 'int inum_full = list->listfull->inum; if (list->ghost) inum_full += list->listfull->gnum;' and :79-80 'list->inum = k_list_full->inum; list->gnum = k_list_full->gnum;'.  src/npair_halffull.cpp:72-73 guards the same addition with 'if (!NEWTON)' and :155-157 sets 'list->inum = inum; if (!NEWTON) if (list->ghost) list->gnum = list->listfull->gnum;'.  The CPU header src/npair_halffull.h registers no NP_NEWTON|NP_GHOST halffull style at all, while npair_halffull_kokkos.h:101-149 does.
failure_scenario: A half+ghost neighbor list with newton on built by KOKKOS (halffull/newton/ghost/kk/*) fills half-list entries for ghost i atoms using the newton 'above and to the right' tie-break, which double counts (owner of the ghost stores the same pair) and reports gnum != 0 to consumers that assume newton ghost lists are empty.
suggested_fix: Either guard the ghost extension and gnum assignment with '!NEWTON' as the CPU version does, or remove the NP_NEWTON|NP_GHOST halffull KOKKOS style registrations if that combination is not supported.

summary: The KOKKOS skip build ignores list->molskip entirely and unconditionally dereferences list->iskip / list->ijskip, which are left as null pointers for molecular skip lists.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/npair_skip_kokkos.cpp:75-79 'k_iskip.view_host()(itype) = list->iskip[itype]; ... k_ijskip.view_host()(itype,jtype) = list->ijskip[itype][jtype];' and the kernel at :122 'if (!d_iskip(itype))' / :137 'if (d_ijskip(itype,type(j))) continue;'.  src/neigh_list.cpp:159-171 only allocates iskip/ijskip when '!molskip'.  The CPU base src/npair_skip.cpp:51,78,98-100 reads 'int molskip = list->molskip;' and applies 'if (!molskip && iskip[itype]) continue;' plus the INTRA/INTER molecule tests; the INTEL variant does the same (src/INTEL/npair_skip_intel.cpp:117,149-151).
failure_scenario: pair_style hybrid/molecular (the only setter, src/pair_hybrid_molecular.cpp:48,51) with a KOKKOS sub-style produces a skip list with molskip != 0 and iskip == ijskip == nullptr; NPairSkipKokkos::build() dereferences the null pointers at :76/:78 -> segmentation fault (and even if they were allocated the intra/inter-molecular filtering would be missing).
suggested_fix: Port the molskip logic (sync MOLECULE_MASK, pass atom->molecule into the functor, apply the INTRA/INTER tests) and skip the iskip/ijskip fill when list->molskip is set; alternatively error out for molskip lists in the KOKKOS skip builder.

summary: list->inum is derived by indexing the last work item of the last phase with index h_ssa_phaseLen(...)-1, which is -1 when that phase ended up with no non-empty work items.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/npair_ssa_kokkos.cpp:470-471 'data.neigh_list.inum = h_ssa_itemLoc(ssa_phaseCt-1,h_ssa_phaseLen(ssa_phaseCt-1)-1) + h_ssa_itemLen(ssa_phaseCt-1,h_ssa_phaseLen(ssa_phaseCt-1)-1);'.  d_ssa_phaseLen(workPhase) is overwritten by the device kernel with the COMPACTED work-item count at :652-653 'if (firstTry) { d_ssa_phaseLen(workPhase) = workItem; ... }', where workItem is only incremented when 'inum > inum_start' (:632-636), so it is 0 for a phase in which no atom got a neighbor.  The CPU base accumulates inum directly instead: src/DPD-REACT/npair_half_bin_newton_ssa.cpp:112 'int inum = 0;' ... :244 'list->inum = inum;'.
failure_scenario: An MPI rank whose subdomain holds no local atoms (or whose last work phase has no atom with neighbors) makes h_ssa_phaseLen(ssa_phaseCt-1) == 0, so the code reads d_ssa_itemLoc/itemLen at column -1: out-of-bounds device read and a garbage list->inum that downstream SSA kernels then loop over.
suggested_fix: Guard the expression (use 0 when the phase length is 0), or better, have the kernel reduce the total inum explicitly the way the CPU builder accumulates it.

summary: AtomNeighbors for the destination half list is constructed with d_numneigh(i), which is the not-yet-written (stale/uninitialized) half-list neighbor count.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/npair_halffull_kokkos.cpp:107-108 'const AtomNeighbors neighbors_i = AtomNeighbors(&d_neighbors(i,0),d_numneigh(i), &d_neighbors(i,1)-&d_neighbors(i,0));' - d_numneigh(i) is only assigned at :157 'd_numneigh(i) = n;', and d_numneigh is freshly allocated without initialization in src/KOKKOS/neigh_list_kokkos.cpp:46.
failure_scenario: Reads uninitialized device memory on the first build (harmless today because AtomNeighbors::num_neighs is never read here, but it trips memory checkers and would silently break if the member were ever used).
suggested_fix: Pass 0 (or the parent count d_numneigh_full(i)) instead of d_numneigh(i), or build the AtomNeighbors object after the count is known.

summary: deallocate() passes the plain device Views to memoryKK->destroy_kokkos() instead of the DualViews the buffers were created from, so k_density_fft/k_work1/k_work2 keep holding their allocations.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pppm_kokkos.cpp:906-908 'memoryKK->destroy_kokkos(d_density_fft,density_fft); memoryKK->destroy_kokkos(d_work1,work1); memoryKK->destroy_kokkos(d_work2,work2);' whereas allocate() created them through the DualViews: :835-842 'memoryKK->create_kokkos(k_density_fft,density_fft,nfft_both,...); d_density_fft = k_density_fft.view<DeviceType>(); ... memoryKK->create_kokkos(k_work1,work1,2*nfft_both,...);'.  destroy_kokkos only does 'data = TYPE(); array = nullptr;' (src/KOKKOS/memory_kokkos.h:83-88), so the DualView reference keeps the memory alive until the next create_kokkos overwrites it.
failure_scenario: On PPPMKokkos::init() (which calls deallocate() at :212 and allocate() at :272) the old grid-sized FFT work arrays are still referenced by k_work1/k_work2/k_density_fft while the new ones are allocated -> transient doubling of the FFT buffer footprint; on a memory-tight GPU this is an out-of-memory abort where the CPU build succeeds.
suggested_fix: Pass the DualViews: 'memoryKK->destroy_kokkos(k_density_fft,density_fft);' etc., and reset the derived device views to empty.

summary: k_eatom/k_vatom are destroyed and re-created on every compute() call whenever per-atom energy/virial is requested, instead of only when the existing view is too small.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pppm_kokkos.cpp:576-585 'if (eflag_atom) { memoryKK->destroy_kokkos(k_eatom,eatom); memoryKK->create_kokkos(k_eatom,eatom,maxeatom,"pair:eatom"); d_eatom = k_eatom.view<DeviceType>(); }' with no size test.  Every other KOKKOS style guards it, e.g. src/KOKKOS/pair_lj_cut_kokkos.cpp 'if (k_eatom.extent(0) < maxeatom) { destroy; create; ... } else Kokkos::deep_copy(d_eatom,0.0);', and the CPU base only reallocates when 'atom->nmax > maxeatom' (src/kspace.cpp, KSpace::ev_setup).
failure_scenario: A run with 'compute pe/atom' or 'compute stress/atom' and 'kspace_style pppm/kk' performs two device allocations plus two frees (each an implicit fence) per timestep, which on a GPU costs far more than the kernels themselves.
suggested_fix: Reallocate only when 'k_eatom.extent(0) < maxeatom' and otherwise Kokkos::deep_copy the view to zero.

summary: d_inum is only written by the thread handling ii == num_skip-1, so when num_skip is 0 the previous build's inum is reused for list->inum.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/npair_skip_kokkos.cpp:157-160 'if (final) { if (ii == num_skip-1) d_inum() = inum; }' - with num_skip == 0 the RangePolicy(0,0) runs no iterations, yet :94-97 still reads d_inum into list->inum.  The CPU base src/npair_skip.cpp:62,122 starts from 'int inum = 0;' and always assigns 'list->inum = inum;'.
failure_scenario: A processor whose parent skip list becomes empty (all atoms migrated away) keeps the stale, larger inum from the previous build; consumers then iterate d_ilist beyond the valid range.
suggested_fix: Deep-copy 0 into d_inum before the parallel_scan, or set list->inum = 0 explicitly when num_skip == 0.

summary: The GPU team kernels stage atom tags through a double shared-memory buffer, so tagint values lose precision in LAMMPS_BIGBIG builds and the newton/triclinic (itag+jtag)%2 tie-break can pick the wrong owner.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/npair_kokkos.cpp:665 'other_x[MY_II + 4 * atoms_per_bin] = itag;' and :779 'const tagint jtag = other_x[m + 4 * atoms_per_bin];' (same pattern at :1389/:1507 in build_ItemSizeGPU), where other_x is 'double* other_x' (:634, :1354).  The flat kernel reads the tags exactly: :532 'const tagint jtag = tag(j);'.  With -DLAMMPS_BIGBIG tagint is int64_t (src/lmptype.h) and values above 2^53 are not representable in a double.
failure_scenario: A LAMMPS_BIGBIG run with atom IDs above 2^53 rounds jtag, so 'if (itag > jtag)' and the '(itag+jtag) % 2' parity test can differ between the two owners of an owned/ghost pair -> the pair is either stored twice or not at all in a half/newton/triclinic list.
suggested_fix: Store tags in a separate tagint-typed slice of the shared-memory block (or read tag(j) directly in the tie-break) instead of round-tripping them through double.

summary: The team kernels return from a subset of the block when mbins is not a multiple of BINS_PER_TEAM, so the later __syncthreads_count()/team_barrier() calls are reached by only part of the block.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/npair_kokkos.cpp:630-632 'const int ibin = dev.league_rank()*BINS_PER_TEAM+MY_BIN; if (ibin >= mbins) return;' where MY_BIN = dev.team_rank()/atoms_per_bin varies within the team (BINS_PER_TEAM == factor == 2 whenever atoms_per_bin < 64, see :264).  The block-wide synchronizations at :671 'int test = (__syncthreads_count(i >= 0 && i < nlocal) == 0);' and :737/:760/:833 'dev.team_barrier();' are then executed by only the MY_BIN==0 half of the block.  Same shape at :992 and :1352.
failure_scenario: An odd mbins with atoms_per_bin < 64 leaves the MY_BIN==1 threads exited before the barriers; the collective is formally undefined and __syncthreads_count returns a partial count, which can make the surviving threads take the early-return branch and skip building neighbor lists for that bin.
suggested_fix: Replace the early return with a predicate that keeps all threads participating in the barriers (e.g. set a local 'valid' flag and guard the body with it), or size the league so every team's bins are in range.
